matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and verify that the equality holds; without this check you may produce a syntactically correct but mathematically false equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you have a candidate transformed equation, compute the numeric values of both sides and ensure they match before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation without confirming that the left‑hand side equals the right‑hand side leads to a false solution.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick retains its orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) when moved; you cannot turn a vertical stick into a diagonal or horizontal one, so only moves that preserve orientation are allowed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When selecting a stick to relocate, ensure the target character requires a stick of the same orientation.
matchstick.example: Trying to turn a vertical stick from an ‘I’ into the diagonal part of an ‘X’ would be invalid.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick move may affect at most two distinct characters: the source character loses the stick and the destination character gains it; no other characters may be altered.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a move, identify exactly which character you will take the stick from and which you will add it to, and ensure no other characters change.
matchstick.example: Altering three characters (e.g., changing a V, a +, and an =) in one move exceeds the two‑character limit.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Only certain Roman‑numeral pairs can be changed by moving a single stick while keeping both characters valid (e.g., I↔II↔III, V↔X, L↔I); use these known conversions as the only viable numeral transformations.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a numeral, consider whether it belongs to one of the allowed single‑stick conversion pairs.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn ‘V’ into ‘L’ by moving one stick would produce an invalid shape, whereas V↔X is allowed.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must be a single line beginning with the exact phrase ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the complete transformed equation; any deviation causes the answer to be rejected.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a valid transformed equation, output it using the required prefix and ensure no extra lines or missing parts.
matchstick.example: Providing just ‘IV + VI’ without the required prefix leads to a format error.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Before attempting any move, record the exact sequence of numerals, operators, and spacing as they appear, so you know which characters are available for modification.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, write down the original equation token by token.
matchstick.example: Misreading ‘XV = IV + VI’ as a different sequence could lead to moving sticks from the wrong characters.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’; removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’. This is the only valid vertical‑stick operator conversion.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change ‘+’ to ‘‑’ or vice versa, move a single vertical stick accordingly.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘+’ to ‘‑’ by removing both its vertical and horizontal sticks would violate the single‑stick rule.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: Removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ (turning it into ‘‑’) and adding that vertical stick to a numeral that lacks an ‘I’ can increase its value by one (e.g., turning ‘I’ into ‘II’).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to raise a numeral by one and have a ‘+’ available, move its vertical stick to the numeral.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘+’ into ‘‑’ and adding the vertical to a ‘V’ would create an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Removing one horizontal line from ‘=’ turns it into a minus sign; adding a horizontal line to a minus sign creates an equals sign. No other horizontal‑stick operator changes are allowed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change ‘=’ to ‘‑’ or vice versa, move a single horizontal stick accordingly.
matchstick.example: Removing both horizontal bars from ‘=’ to make ‘‑’ uses two sticks and is invalid.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A V can be turned into an X (and vice versa) by moving a single diagonal stick within the same character; this conversion does not require any other character to change and preserves the total stick count.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a V that, if turned into X, would balance the arithmetic, consider repositioning one of its diagonal sticks to create an X.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V unchanged when converting it to X would keep the equation false.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may focus on the visual transformation and assume the resulting equation is correct without checking the numeric values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the integer values of both sides of the transformed equation and confirm they are equal before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may ignore the requirement that the resulting character must correspond to a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that both the source (after losing a stick) and destination (after gaining a stick) still represent recognized Roman numerals or operators.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may add or remove sticks in a way that changes an operator into a shape that is not a defined operator (e.g., turning '+' into a non‑standard symbol).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Restrict operator changes to the documented conversions (plus↔minus via vertical stick, equals↔minus via horizontal stick).

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from a character but does not place it onto another character, violating the rule that the stick must be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When you take a stick from a source character, immediately decide on a valid destination character and add the stick there.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may output the transformed equation without the required prefix or on multiple lines, causing the parser to reject it.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Output exactly one line that starts with 'Correct version of the equation:' followed by the full equation, with no extra text.
